title: Iterated residue reduction and direct reduction have the same zero cohomology
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, X a scheme, K any object in the derived category of modules over the completed integral coefficient sheaf, and n a natural number (representing exponent n+1). Let L represent its finite reduction K_n, via an isomorphism Q(L) ≅ K_n, and let f : P → L be any quasi-isomorphism with P K-flat over A_(n+1). Then in every degree i the underlying A_(n+1)-cohomology of the chosen derived tensor L tensor^L_(A_(n+1)) (A_(n+1)/(uniformizer)) is zero if and only if the A_1-cohomology of the direct level-one reduction of K is zero. No constructibility, completeness or cohomological bound is assumed.

source.place: Proof; K-flat realization of coefficient tensor associativity

proof.text: Identify any ordinary scalar-extension functor with the ordinary part of a normalized presentation using its prescribed object and map equations. Uniqueness of left derived functors identifies the integral reduction functors with the normalized derived presentations. The normalized composition isomorphism and the inverse-limit cone equations compare extension of the finite reduction to the first quotient with direct first reduction. The cone equation follows by induction on n from the successive coefficient transitions.

source.place: Proof; K-flat realization of coefficient tensor associativity

proof.text: The image of the first uniformizer ideal in A_(n+1) is the ideal generated by its uniformizer class. The quotient-of-quotient ring equivalence identifies this residue quotient with A_1 and respects the quotient maps. Apply the constant sheaf functor and construct the induced isomorphism of the two regular modules restricted to A_(n+1), sectionwise by the ring equivalence.

source.place: Proof; K-flat realization of coefficient tensor associativity

proof.text: Use the universal derived counit to compute the finite-to-first extension on the supplied K-flat complex P; transport along the quasi-isomorphism P to L. Tensor cancellation with the regular target module identifies restricted ordinary extension with left tensor by its restricted regular module, naturally in the input. Pass this natural isomorphism to complexes. Tensor symmetry and the tensor-with-a-single-complex isomorphism identify that complex with the given derivedTensorRing model. Transport its second factor using the regular-module isomorphism of the preceding step.

source.place: Proof; K-flat realization of coefficient tensor associativity

proof.text: Restriction of scalars is exact because its composite with the forgetful functor is the unchanged underlying abelian sheaf functor. It is faithful for the same reason. The exact-functor homology isomorphism, and faithfulness applied to the identity morphism, show that restricted derived cohomology is zero exactly when the original cohomology is zero. Combine this with the composition and tensor-model isomorphisms in every degree.

theorem integralReduction_residue_homology_zero_iff
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u})
    (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E X)) (n : ℕ)
    (L P : CochainComplex (scalarReductionTarget.{u, u} l E X n) ℤ)
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅ (scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E X n).obj K)
    (f : P ⟶ L) (hf : QuasiIso f)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat.{u + 1, u}
      (R := integralCoefficientCommRingSheaf.{u, u} l E X n) P)
    (i : ℤ) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (scalarReductionTarget.{u, u} l E X n) i).obj
        (derivedTensorRing.{u} X (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))
          (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1) ⧸ Ideal.span
            {Ideal.Quotient.mk (Padic.coefficientExtensionIdeal l E (n + 1))
              (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E)})
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk _) L P f hf hP)) ↔
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (scalarReductionTarget.{u, u} l E X 0) i).obj
        ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension.{u, u} l E X 0).obj K))
